subject: Sentinel: urgent request for incident logs and audit evidence
messages:
From: Allen Tay <allen.tay@sentinelbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: Latency spike 2026-11-21 08:40-09:05 PT — request for logs/evidence

Hi Karthik,

We observed a sustained latency and elevated 5xx rate hitting our production integration with Redwood between ~08:40-09:05 PT this morning (11/21). Impact: intermittent request timeouts for ~20% of user requests for a subset of routes (chat-generation /model:open-embed). Our security and incident teams are asking for the following evidence for our internal postmortem and audit:

- Full request/response logs (redacted if necessary) for 08:30-09:15 PT
- Service-level runtime traces and trace IDs (span-level if available)
- Any automatic fallback or model variant routing logs during the window
- Aggregated token usage and error-rate breakdown by route/model
- Confirmation of where logs are retained and for how long (S3/Data store path)

This is currently escalating to our CIO and security (cc'ing security@sentinelbank.com). Please confirm you will preserve relevant artifacts and provide an ETA for a packaged evidence delivery and the chain-of-custody.

We need this for potential regulatory review; please treat as urgent.

Thanks,
Allen
Allen Tay
Incident Lead — Platform Reliability
Sentinel Bank
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Allen Tay <allen.tay@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike 2026-11-21 08:40-09:05 PT — request for logs/evidence

Allen — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We will preserve the requested artifacts immediately. Can you confirm the exact routes and model names you saw impacted (example: /v1/chat/generate model-id: rwd-4b-open-v1) and the time zone you prefer (I've used PT below)?

Action items from our side (initial):
- Preservation hold: we will place an internal legal/ops hold on all runtime logs for 08:30–09:15 PT.
- Artifact collection: infra team will bundle runtime traces, request/response pairs (where retained), and routing decisions.
- CS/AE contact: looping in Marissa for coordination on delivery and sensitive-data scoping.
- Legal/Compliance: Monica on the thread for preservation notice and chain-of-custody.

Marissa/Monica: please confirm what we can provide by EOD and if you need any additional scope from Allen.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Allen Tay <allen.tay@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike 2026-11-21 08:40-09:05 PT — request for logs/evidence

Allen — I pulled the incident window and started assembling an inventory. Quick answers first: yes, we will preserve artifacts; we can provide a packaged evidence bundle with preliminary items by tomorrow morning. Below is the draft inventory we will collect (we'll mark PII-sensitive items and redact where required):

Preliminary artifact inventory (will include metadata fields and timestamps):
- Runtime access logs (tokenized request IDs, route path, timestamp) — 08:30–09:15 PT
- Request/response pairs where stored (payloads may contain user data) — will flag for scoping
- Traces and spans (Jaeger-style traces) with trace IDs — spans, latencies, error flags
- Model routing logs (fallbacks, variant swaps, region routing)
- Autoscaling and capacity events for Dedicated pools (if relevant)
- KV-cache snapshot markers and cache-hit metrics (if a cache eviction correlated)
- Aggregated metrics: 5xx rates, p99/p95 latency by route/model
- Token usage summary (per-route, per-client)

Attachments: incident_artifact_inventory.csv (small manifest) — see attached.

Jonas: can you confirm the S3 archive path and whether we should produce a single WORM export vs. a secured zipped package for transfer?

Allen — can you confirm whether you require raw payloads, or if redacted/pseudonymized payloads suffice? Also let us know if you have a preferred secure transfer method (SFTP/secure share/DocuSign Transfer link).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_artifact_inventory.csv (CSV, 6KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Allen Tay <allen.tay@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike 2026-11-21 08:40-09:05 PT — preservation notice and chain-of-custody

Allen / Sentinel security team —

This email serves as Redwood's formal preservation notice for the artifacts described by Marissa for the window 2026-11-21 08:30–09:15 PT. We will:

1) Immediately apply a legal/ops hold to prevent deletion/rotation of runtime logs, traces, and related telemetry.
2) Export a time-scoped, read-only WORM archive to a segregated S3 bucket (encrypted with customer-specific KMS key).
3) Produce an evidence manifest that enumerates files, checksums (SHA256), and relevant metadata.
4) Maintain an access log for any internal access to the evidence and provide chain-of-custody entries.

Chain-of-custody and delivery options:
- Preferred: secure, time-limited S3 presigned download (TLS) + delivery manifest and signed CoC PDF (we can provide a signed CoC template).
- Alternative: SFTP account provisioning to a pre-approved host (we will share IP allowlist).
- For highly sensitive payloads, we can produce redacted exports and then run a joint review before delivering raw payloads.

Please advise if your legal or security teams require additional certifications (SOC 2 scoped evidence, notarized signatures) or if a third-party forensic ingestion format is required. We will not release raw user payloads without an explicit scope and an approved NDA/amendment.

Attachments: preservation_notice.docx (word doc, 12KB); chain_of_custody_template.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sentinel Security <security@sentinelbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike 2026-11-21 08:40-09:05 PT — preservation notice and chain-of-custody

Karthik / Marissa / Monica — thanks for the quick response and the preservation notice. A few clarifications so we can scope our postmortem and any regulatory reporting:

- We require the full request/response pairs for 08:35–09:00 PT unredacted to validate transaction-level failure patterns. If Redwood policy prevents full raw payload transfer, please advise what redaction fields are applied by default.
- Please include trace IDs and a mapping to any CDN/proxy hops; if you can provide span-level timings that will help correlate with our internal telemetry.
- We prefer SFTP to a dedicated host with an allowlisted Redwood IP and a time-limited account. If you prefer presigned S3 links, share the required IAM role/permissions and the expected expiry.
- ETA: can you confirm when the evidence bundle will be available (initial package and final package post-redaction)?

Requesting a formal chain-of-custody PDF and the SHA256 manifest. If you can provide an estimated timeline by EOD PT, that will help us align the Sentinel exec briefing.

Allen (cc) — standing by for any additional channel-specific instructions.

Thanks,
Sentinel Security
security@sentinelbank.com
